details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py:137-152 | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: cmd_pack computes the chunk count without enforcing MAX_CHUNKS_PER_MANIFEST, so oversized V2 state can be written in a format the extractor rejects.
  WHY: All reviewers report the writer/reader contract mismatch; extract already rejects total > MAX_CHUNKS_PER_MANIFEST, so packed state can become permanently unreadable and fall back to stale V1.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1041-1098 | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: post_state_comment returns failure on V2 persistence errors without a V1 fallback, and callers swallow that failure with || true.
  WHY: All reviewers say V2 write failures can leave no new persisted state, so later polls reread stale comments and may repeat completed work.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1178-1182 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The V2 extractor's stderr is redirected to /dev/null, discarding diagnostics on plumbing failures.
  WHY: Reviewers agree operators only see the eventual V1 fallback and lose the specific JSON/file/UTF-8 error that would explain why V2 extraction failed.
- scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py:119-138 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: _looks_like_re_escape_output can misclassify valid re.escape output containing backslash-digit sequences as not escape-like.
  WHY: Both reviewers describe the round-trip heuristic as a Python re.sub backreference footgun that leaves some satisfiable substring-filter cases unpruned.
- scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh:67-78 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The greedy sed replacement can strip legitimate trailing edit claims after the first reference clause.
  WHY: Both reviewers say multi-edit bullets can lose later claims, which can produce false EDITOR_CHANGES_LOST results.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:754-774 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: Exit 137 can be misclassified because the timeout/OOM distinction relies on elapsed seconds rather than the actual signal cause.
  WHY: Both reviewers report that external SIGKILL/OOM cases can be routed to the timeout path or otherwise give misleading retry guidance.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:920-930 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The no-progress check compares sorted violation files with cmp, which can mis-handle output-order changes between attempts.
  WHY: Both reviewers say the logic assumes stable verifier output and can abort or mis-detect progress when emitted ordering changes.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:700/3726 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The 170-minute step cap leaves little slack for the three 50-minute attempts plus cleanup/validation.
  WHY: Both reviewers state the budget is tight enough that a long final attempt can be SIGKILLed before EXIT-trap dispatch.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1169-1209 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The V2 extraction path enforces an 8 MiB payload cap only after stitching comments, so oversized or forged manifests still incur full extraction work first.
  WHY: This reviewer says the rejection happens post-stitch, wasting CPU/RAM before the fallback to V1.
- scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py:230-231 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: cmd_extract rejects UTF-8 BOM-prefixed comments JSON because it reads text with encoding="utf-8" and then json.loads the string.
  WHY: The reviewer says a BOM-containing payload would raise JSONDecodeError and force silent fallback to V1.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:6318-6440 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The PR still lacks a dedicated test for the new pack-side guard that should reject chunk counts above MAX_CHUNKS_PER_MANIFEST.
  WHY: The reviewer says the existing V2 parsing tests do not exercise this specific failure path, so the writer/reader mismatch remains untested.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py:137-152 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: cmd_pack computes total chunks without checking MAX_CHUNKS_PER_MANIFEST, but cmd_extract rejects chains where total exceeds that limit.
  WHY: A sufficiently large state snapshot can be posted successfully and then become permanently unreadable, forcing fallback to stale V1 state.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1041-1098 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: post_state_comment has V2 failure paths that return 1 without a V1 fallback, and callers use post_state_comment || true.
  WHY: When V2 persistence fails, the next poll cycle rereads stale persisted state and can re-execute already completed work.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1178-1182 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The V2 extraction invocation suppresses stderr from the Python extractor with 2>/dev/null.
  WHY: Plumbing failures lose their specific diagnostics, so operators only see the eventual V1 fallback behavior.
- scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py:119-138 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The round-trip heuristic in _looks_like_re_escape_output can mis-handle backslash-digit sequences and reject valid re.escape-like patterns.
  WHY: The false negative leaves some satisfiable must_not_contain/must_contain pairs unpruned and degrades resolver effectiveness.
